summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identity via npm install hooks
details: The scoped package @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics declares all three npm lifecycle scripts (preinstall, install, postinstall) to run poc.js. On install, poc.js collects host-identifying data — hostname, username, platform, current working directory, Node.js version, package version, and the names of CI-related environment variables — and transmits it to external out-of-band collectors over HTTP GET and as DNS labels. The traced destinations are a subdomain under oast.fun (db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun) and a nip.io-wrapped IP (80-190-83-27.nip.io). The scoped name targets an internal namespace, so any build that misresolves the scope against the public registry pulls this package and executes the beacon on the installer's machine. The lifecycle-hook delivery channel is arbitrary-code execution; the currently shipped payload is reconnaissance, but the mechanism allows any future payload. A self-description as an authorized proof-of-concept does not alter the on-install behavior for any installer that resolves the name.
